title: Jelly Mug & Bouncy ShaderBall Collision Lab
description: A coffee mug made of soft jelly-like material sits on a table while a bouncy ShaderBall can be launched at it. The user controls launch angle, velocity, and the softness parameters of both objects, watching them deform, wobble, and settle through simulated soft-body physics. The goal is to knock the jelly mug off the table edge by tuning parameters across multiple steps.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a soft-body collision lab. Load coffeeMug.glb and place it near the edge of a wooden-textured rectangular table (BoxGeometry). Load ShaderBall.glb and position it on the left side as a projectile. Both objects should have vertex-displacement-based soft-body simulation: store original vertex positions, and on collision or impact, displace vertices radially from the contact point, then spring them back over time using a damped harmonic oscillator per vertex. Provide a dat.GUI panel (CDN) with these controls: (1) Launch Angle slider 0-60 degrees, (2) Launch Velocity slider 1-20, (3) Mug Stiffness slider 0.1-2.0 controlling spring constant, (4) Mug Damping slider 0.01-0.5, (5) Ball Stiffness slider 0.1-2.0, (6) Ball Damping slider 0.01-0.5, (7) Gravity slider 1-20, (8) a Launch button that fires the ShaderBall toward the mug. On launch, animate the ShaderBall along a parabolic arc influenced by gravity. On collision (bounding-sphere intersection), apply vertex deformation to both meshes proportional to relative velocity and inversely proportional to stiffness. The mug should slide toward the table edge if hit hard enough; if its center passes the edge, it tumbles off with rotation. Display a status text overlay showing deformation magnitude, mug position, and whether the mug fell off. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 4, 8) looking at the table center. Add OrbitControls for free viewing. Lighting: one DirectionalLight with shadows enabled, one HemisphereLight for ambient fill. The table should receive shadows. Add a ground plane below the table. Include a Reset button to restore both objects to original positions and vertex states. Validate that stiffness values stay above 0.1 to prevent instability. The interaction flow requires at least 6 steps: adjust angle, set velocity, tune mug softness, tune ball softness, launch, then reset or re-tune and relaunch to achieve the knock-off goal.
